input.content:
# Switchboard

A shared team inbox. Customers write to a business through a messaging provider
(Pigeon), support agents sign in, see conversations arrive live, claim them and
reply. Several workspaces share one deployment and never see each other's data.

Stack: Node 22, Express 5, TypeScript, MongoDB, Redis, `ws`. The web app is
React + Vite.

## Run it

You need Node 22+ and Docker.

```
npm run up                  # MongoDB, Redis, Pigeon, IdP, Paybox in Docker
npm run scaffold:install    # server and web dependencies
npm run scaffold:server     # API on http://localhost:4000
npm run scaffold:web        # web app on http://localhost:5173
```

Settings come from the environment; the defaults match the local Docker
services, so no `.env` is needed. `.env.example` lists every variable.
`GRADER_TOKEN` must be set explicitly when `NODE_ENV=production`.

No Docker: `npm run mocks` starts the simulators with plain Node, and
`MONGO_URL` / `REDIS_URL` can point at any MongoDB and Redis.

## Check

```
npm run check               # level 1, about 90 s
npm run check:full          # levels 1, 2, 3 and 5, about 4 min, writes CHECK_REPORT.json
npm run check -- --levels 5
```

The check starts the server itself (see `switchboard.json`), so stop your dev
server first. It wipes application data.

## How it is put together

```
Pigeon --webhook--> POST /webhooks/pigeon --> MongoDB (messages, frames)
                                                  |
                          Redis pub/sub  <--------+
                                |
browser <--WebSocket /ws--------+

agent reply --> outbox (MongoDB) --> sender loop --> Pigeon /v1/messages
```

- **Webhooks** (`routes/webhook.ts`): HMAC signature over the raw body, five
  minute window. A message is stored first and acknowledged after, so a
  crash makes Pigeon retry. Inserts are keyed on Pigeon's `message_id`, so
  duplicates collapse. Order is by `occurred_at`, not arrival.
- **Frames** (`lib/frames.ts`): every change a client may care about is a row
  with a per-workspace `seq`, written under a short Redis lock so rows commit
  in seq order. WebSocket clients read rows after their last seq, which is
  also how `?after=` replay works.
- **Replies** (`lib/outbox.ts`): a reply is a row in `outbox`, written before
  the request is answered. Any server copy can lease a due row (20 s lease),
  so work left by a dead copy is picked up by the others. Pigeon gets the
  `client_ref` as `Idempotency-Key`, which makes every retry safe.
- **Rate limit** (`lib/ratelimit.ts`): one token bucket per workspace in
  Redis, shared by all copies. A `429 Retry-After` or `503` pauses the
  workspace for everyone.
- **Claim** (`lib/conversations.ts`): one atomic upsert guarded by a unique
  index on `(workspace, contact)`, so only one agent can hold a conversation.

## Layout

```
scaffold/server/src
  index.ts            wiring, health, shutdown
  config.ts           environment
  db.ts               collections and indexes
  routes/             webhook, grader (check endpoints)
  lib/                signature, frames, inbound, outbox, ratelimit, conversations
harness/              the check (given)
pigeon/ idp/ paybox/  simulators (given)
```

`DECISIONS.md` has what was cut and what is still wrong.

input.prompt:
Build the React frontend for "Switchboard", a shared team inbox, in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/web (Vite + React 19 + TypeScript, already scaffolded; deps installed; only edit files inside scaffold/web, do NOT touch scaffold/server or the repo root). Do not run `npm run check` or the harness; do not start the Docker stack.

Style rules (important): write plain, human-looking code. No emoji, no banner comments, no "// This component..." narration; at most a short comment where something is non-obvious. Small focused components in src/components, a tiny api helper, one hook for the socket, one plain CSS file (no UI libraries, no CSS frameworks). Readable names, no over-abstraction.

Backend contract (server on :4000, Vite already proxies /api /auth /ws to it; cookie session `sb_sid`, httpOnly, so always fetch with same-origin default credentials):
- GET /auth/login  -> browser navigation (full page redirect) starts login; after login the server redirects to the web origin (/).
- POST /auth/logout -> {ok:true}
- GET /api/me -> 200 { sub, name, email, workspaces:[{id, role:'admin'|'agent'}] } or 401 (not signed in).
- GET /api/conversations?workspace=<id>&status=open|closed&assignee=me&limit=30&before=<cursor> -> { conversations:[{contact, assignee|null, status:'open'|'closed', lastActivityAt, preview}], next: cursor|null }  (newest activity first; pass `next` back as `before` to load more)
- GET /api/conversations/:contact/messages?workspace=<id>&limit=50&before=<iso> -> { conversation:{contact,assignee,status}|null, messages:[{direction:'in'|'out', id, text, at, status?:'queued'|'sent'|'delivered'|'failed', sender?}] oldest first, older: iso|null }  (`id` is Pigeon message_id for inbound, client_ref for outbound; `older` is the `before` value for loading earlier messages). Contact is a phone number like +14155550101: URL-encode it in the path.
- POST /api/conversations/:contact/reply  body {workspace, text, clientRef} -> 202 {clientRef}. Generate clientRef in the browser with crypto.randomUUID() when the agent presses send, show the message immediately as 'queued', and if the request fails to get an answer retry once with the SAME clientRef (the server dedupes on it).
- POST /api/conversations/:contact/claim body {workspace} -> 200 {result:'claimed'|'already'} or 409 when someone else holds it.
- POST /api/conversations/:contact/release body {workspace} -> 200 | 409.
- POST /api/conversations/:contact/close and /reopen body {workspace} -> {changed:boolean}.
- All POSTs send content-type application/json.
- WebSocket: `ws(s)://<host>/ws?workspace=<id>&after=<lastSeq>` (same origin through the Vite proxy, cookie auth). Text frames are JSON, each with an increasing integer `seq`. Types: {type:'message.inbound', contact, message_id, text, occurred_at}, {type:'message.outbound', contact, client_ref, text, sender, status}, {type:'message.status', contact, client_ref, status}, {type:'conversation.assigned', contact, assignee|null}, {type:'conversation.status', contact, status}. Keep the highest seq seen per workspace; on close, reconnect with exponential backoff (1s up to ~10s) passing after=<lastSeq> so nothing is missed; ignore frames with seq <= lastSeq. Status only moves forward: queued < sent < delivered/failed (a late 'sent' must not overwrite 'delivered').

Product to build:
1. Signed-out screen with a "Sign in" button (links to /auth/login). While /api/me loads show a minimal loader. After sign in show the app.
2. Top bar: app name, workspace switcher if the user has more than one workspace (user u_eli has two), the user's name, sign out. Re-open the socket when the workspace changes. Remember last workspace in localStorage.
3. Left column: inbox list with filter tabs (Open / Closed / Mine), contacts newest activity first, each row showing contact, preview, relative time, assignee badge. "Load more" using `next`. List updates live from socket frames (new inbound moves a conversation to the top and refreshes preview; assignment and status frames update the badge). If a frame references a contact not in the list, refetch the first page.
4. Right column: the selected conversation as a thread (inbound left, outbound right), oldest at top, auto-scroll to bottom for new messages unless the user scrolled up, "Load earlier" using `older`. Outbound bubbles show their status (queued/sent/delivered/failed) with a small label and a distinct failed style. Header with contact, assignee, buttons: Claim (disabled and labelled with the holder when held by someone else; if the server answers 409 show "already claimed by someone else" and refresh), Release (only when I hold it, or admin), Close / Reopen.
5. Reply box under the thread: textarea, Enter sends, Shift+Enter newline, disabled while empty, max 4000 chars.
6. Small, honest empty/error states (network error banner, "no conversations yet"). Responsive enough for a laptop; no need for mobile polish.
7. Use semantic HTML and keyboard-reachable controls, visible focus styles, labels on inputs.

Verify: run `cd /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build` and fix everything until both pass (delete the generated dist/ afterwards; it is gitignored but keep the tree tidy). You cannot sign in through a browser, so also re-read your socket/reconnect and status-merge logic once for bugs. Final report (under 250 words): files created, any contract assumption you had to make, and anything you could not verify.

input.description: Build E2E encrypted notes UI + protocol doc
input.prompt:
Add end-to-end encrypted private notes to the Switchboard web app in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/web (React 19 + Vite + TS, no extra libraries: use the browser WebCrypto API only), and write /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/PROTOCOL.md. Only edit files in scaffold/web/src and that one markdown file. Do not touch scaffold/server, do not run the harness or docker. Existing code to read first: src/components/Thread.tsx, Workspace.tsx, src/api.ts, src/types.ts, src/useSocket.ts, src/styles.css.

Style rules: plain human-looking code, no emoji, no narration comments, short comments only where non-obvious, small files (src/crypto.ts for primitives, src/keyring.ts for key management, src/components/NotesPanel.tsx for UI), reuse the existing api helper and CSS conventions (extend styles.css with a few rules).

Goal: agents leave private notes on a conversation for the other agents in the same workspace. The server must NOT be able to read them.

Scheme (implement exactly this):
- Each user has an ECDH P-256 keypair per workspace, generated in the browser. The private key is stored in IndexedDB as a non-extractable CryptoKey (DB 'switchboard-keys', key by `${sub}:${workspace}`); the public key is exported as SPKI and sent base64 (standard base64, no padding issues: the server accepts [A-Za-z0-9+/_-] plus up to two '=').
- Each workspace has one random AES-GCM 256 key K (the 'workspace key'). K is stored on the server only wrapped: for a recipient, derive a wrap key via ECDH(my private, recipient public) -> HKDF-SHA256 (salt empty, info 'switchboard-wrap-v1') -> AES-GCM 256; encrypt the raw K bytes with a random 12-byte IV; the wrappedKey string is base64(iv || ciphertext). To unwrap, derive the same way using ECDH(my private, wrapper's public key) where the wrapper is `wrappedBy` (a user sub, look up its publicKey from the members list). A user who wraps K for themselves uses their own public key (wrappedBy = own sub).
- A note is AES-GCM encrypted with K, random 12-byte IV, plaintext = UTF-8 text, additionalData = UTF-8 of `${workspace}|${contact}|${author}` so a note cannot be moved to another conversation or attributed to another user. Sent as {ciphertext: base64, iv: base64}.
- Cache the unwrapped K in memory only (module scope), never persist it.

Server API (all under the session cookie, JSON, POSTs/PUTs send content-type application/json; errors are {error:string}):
- PUT /api/keys {workspace, publicKey} -> {ok:true}. Registers my public key for the workspace (replacing it invalidates the key wrapped for the old one, so only call it when no local keypair exists).
- GET /api/workspaces/:ws/keys -> { initialised:boolean, members:[{sub, publicKey, hasKey:boolean}], mine: {wrappedKey, wrappedBy} | null }.
- POST /api/workspaces/:ws/keyring {wrappedKey} -> 201 | 409 (already initialised, or I have not registered a public key). Creates the workspace key: only call when initialised is false; generate K, wrap for myself, post. On 409 reload state.
- PUT /api/workspaces/:ws/keys/:sub {wrappedKey} -> 200 | 403 (I do not hold K) | 409 (target unknown or already has a key). Used to share K with a member who registered a key but has hasKey false. (:sub is a user id like u_ben, encode it.)
- POST /api/conversations/:contact/notes {workspace, ciphertext, iv} -> 201 {id}.
- GET /api/conversations/:contact/notes?workspace=<id> -> {notes:[{id, author, ciphertext, iv, createdAt}]} oldest first. Contact is a phone number like +14155550101: URL-encode in the path.
- WebSocket frame {seq, type:'note.added', contact, note_id, author} arrives on the existing socket (add it to the Frame union in types.ts); on it, if it is for the open conversation, refetch notes.

Behaviour of the notes panel (inside the thread view, e.g. a collapsible 'Private notes' section under the header or beside the messages; label it clearly as encrypted and visible only to the workspace's agents):
1. On open: if no local keypair, generate one and PUT /api/keys. Fetch key state. If I have `mine`, unwrap K and show/decrypt notes. If not and !initialised, create the keyring (generate K). If not and initialised, show 'Waiting for a teammate to share the workspace key' and poll the key state every 5 s.
2. Any member who holds K should, whenever they load key state and see members with hasKey=false, wrap K for each of them and PUT it (silently, do this in keyring.ts as `shareWithPending`; call it from the panel on load and on a 10 s interval while the panel is mounted, and also when the workspace has pending members after the Workspace mounts is NOT required).
3. Decrypt failures (tampered or wrong key) show 'Could not decrypt this note' for that note, not a crash. Show author (resolve to the sub; 'You' for me) and time.
4. Compose box: textarea + 'Add note'; encrypt then POST; show the new note after the notes refetch.
5. If IndexedDB or crypto.subtle is unavailable (non-secure context) show a clear message instead of failing. Note localhost counts as secure.

PROTOCOL.md (for the assessment reviewers; it should be concrete and honest, around 1 to 1.5 pages): who holds which key (user ECDH private key: only in that user's browser, non-extractable IndexedDB; workspace key K: only in browsers, wrapped per member on the server; server holds public keys, wrapped keys, ciphertext, IVs, author id, timestamps, contact id), the exact flows (join, first-member bootstrap, sharing K, writing and reading a note, what the AAD binds), what the server can and cannot do, and exactly THREE attacks the scheme does NOT stop, stated plainly with consequences. Use these three: (1) a malicious or compromised server can substitute a member's public key when K is shared (there is no out-of-band fingerprint verification), then wrap K to itself via a fake member and read all later notes and the existing ones it is given; (2) no forward secrecy or key rotation and no revocation: someone removed from the workspace keeps K and any ciphertext they copied, and a new member who is given K can read all old notes; (3) the server can delete, withhold, or replay notes and cannot be detected (no signature or sequence binding between notes; AAD stops moving across conversations but not dropping or duplicating within one), plus metadata (who wrote, when, how long, which contact) is visible to the server; also mention that XSS in the web app would expose usable keys in the page and that a lost browser profile means lost access. Also state first-write-wins on keys and that an existing holder can be tricked only by the server substituting keys (same as attack 1).

Verify: `cd /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build`, then delete dist/. Also write a small Node script test-free check: add src/crypto.test.ts is NOT needed, but do exercise your crypto.ts primitives once in Node (Node 22 has globalThis.crypto.subtle) with a throwaway script run via `npx tsx` (import crypto.ts, wrap K for a recipient and unwrap, encrypt/decrypt a note, confirm decrypt fails with a wrong AAD), then delete the throwaway script. Keep crypto.ts free of DOM/IndexedDB imports so that works (put IndexedDB code in keyring.ts). Final report (under 250 words): files, anything you assumed, anything unverified.

input.content:
# Decisions

## What is built

- Webhook ingest with signature and replay checks, idempotent by Pigeon id, ordered by `occurred_at`.
- Replies through an outbox in MongoDB, sent by a loop that any server copy can run. Pigeon gets the `client_ref` as `Idempotency-Key`.
- Per-workspace rate limit and `Retry-After` pause shared through Redis.
- OIDC login (code + PKCE, id_token verified against the IdP's JWKS), sessions in Redis, workspace membership checked on every API call and on the WebSocket.
- Inbox API with cursor pagination, claim / release / close / reopen, WebSocket with `seq` and `?after=` replay.
- React app for all of the above.
- Encrypted private notes (`PROTOCOL.md`).
- Tests for the signature check, claim race, frame ordering, rate limiter and the notes/key endpoints (`npm --prefix scaffold/server test`, needs MongoDB and Redis).

## What is cut

- Search (Elasticsearch). Not started.
- Billing bonus. Not started.
- No frontend tests; the app is only type-checked and built.

## Choices where the brief is silent

- Every change a client may need is a row in `frames` with a per-workspace `seq`. The WebSocket reads rows after the client's last `seq`; Redis pub/sub only wakes sockets up, so a lost pub/sub message costs at most 2 seconds.
- `seq` is assigned under a short Redis lock so rows commit in order. The unique `(workspace, seq)` index is what really guarantees uniqueness if the lock ever expires.
- A message from a customer reopens a closed conversation.
- `assignee` is the IdP `sub`. The check's `agent` is stored as given.
- Any 2xx from Pigeon counts as accepted. A 4xx other than 429 marks the reply `failed`; 5xx, 408, timeouts and network errors are retried with backoff forever.
- A lease of 20 s on an outbox row is how a dead copy's work is picked up. Failover therefore takes up to about 20 s.
- Message status only moves forward (queued, sent, delivered or failed).

## What I know is still wrong or weak

- Replies to the same contact can leave in a different order than they were typed if one of them is retried.
- Assign / close frames are written after the database update. If the process dies in between, the frame is missing until the same agent repeats the action. A client that reconnects and refetches still sees the right state.
- A customer message that is stored but whose process dies before the conversation is reopened will not reopen it when Pigeon retries (the retry sees the message already stored).
- `frames` is never cleaned up.
- Level 4 is not in the local check. I went through the answer table in `PIGEON.md` by hand and by sending those requests, but I have not seen it scored.
- The web app has not been used in a real browser by anyone but me on my own machine; layout and scrolling are the likeliest places for rough edges.
- Secrets default to the dev values when the environment is empty. The server refuses to start in production without `GRADER_TOKEN`, but not for the others.

content.content:
1:# Private notes: encryption protocol
5:## Who holds what
17:## Flows
23:**Sharing K.** Any member holding K, on panel load and every 10 s, looks for members with `hasKey = false` and `PUT`s a wrapped K for each. Wrapping: `ECDH(my private, recipient public)` -> HKDF-SHA256 (empty salt, info `switchboard-wrap-v1`) -> AES-GCM 256 key; encrypt raw K with a random 12-byte IV; `wrappedKey = base64(iv || ciphertext)`. A member without K shows "Waiting for a teammate to share the workspace key" and polls every 5 s. To unwrap, the recipient derives the same key from `ECDH(my private, wrappedBy's public)`, with the wrapper's public key taken from the members list the server returns.
29:## What the server can and cannot do
35:## Attacks this scheme does NOT stop
43:Also out of scope: XSS in the web app can use the keys in the page (the private key is non-extractable, but the page can still ask the browser to use it, and K is in memory); and losing the browser profile (IndexedDB cleared, new device) loses the private key. Access is regained by registering a new public key (the server then drops the key that was wrapped for the old one) and having a teammate who holds K share it again.

| Commit | Kya hai |
|---|---|
| `6696c7f` | Server: webhook, outbox, rate limit, claim |

## Abhi push hona baaki hai
- **Frontend** (inbox, thread, reply, claim, live updates). Ye `gohlai-assessment` me rakha hai par commit nahi hua.
- **Encrypted notes:** server routes, browser crypto, `PROTOCOL.md`.
- **Server tests** (28).
- **`DECISIONS.md`**, README ka update, aur final `CHECK_REPORT.json`.

## Ek cheez ki clarity
Ye sab **seedhe `main` branch pe commit ho raha hai**, Pull Request (PR) nahi ban raha. Tumhare assessment ke liye ye theek hai, kyunki wo "repository ka commit" dekhte hain, PR nahi. Agar tum PR flow chahte ho (branch banakar PR), to bata do.

## Abhi kya chal raha hai
Final full check level 2 pe hai, level 3 aur 5 baaki hain. Aakhri result aate hi main commits push karne ke liye tumse confirm maangunga, aur phir ek ke baad ek 4 commits daalunga (web, server notes + tests, web notes + `PROTOCOL.md`, docs + check report).
server notes and web notes kya hai? ye required hai ?

Nahi, ye **required nahi hai**. BRIEF.md me ye "Also valued (reviewed, not checked automatically)" wale hisse me hai, yaani optional.

## Ye hai kya
Agents conversation pe ek **private note** chhod sakte hain, jo sirf usi workspace ke dusre agents padh sakte hain. Khaas baat ye hai ki **server ye note padh nahi sakta**.

- **Server notes:** server sirf ulta-seedha (encrypted) text store karta hai aur wapas deta hai. Isme keys register karne aur notes save/list karne ke routes hain.
- **Web notes:** browser me hi note encrypt aur decrypt hota hai, aur keys bhi wahin bante hain. Ye `NotesPanel` ke andar kaam karta hai.
- **`PROTOCOL.md`:** ek chhoti file jisme likha hai kaun si key kiske paas hai, aur 3 attacks jo ye design nahi rokta.

## Isse kya milta hai
- BRIEF me "Security beyond the check" ke **4 points** me "encrypted notes if attempted" ka zikr hai. Matlab iska kuch hissa wahan count hota hai.
- `PROTOCOL.md` sirf tab chahiye jab tumne notes try kiye ho.
- 85 points wale automatic check me ye **nahi** aata. Wahan tumhara 75/75 iske bina bhi pakka hai.

## Dhyan rakhne wali baat
- Follow-up call me wo tumhare code ke baare me poochhenge. Notes me crypto hai (key wrap, AES-GCM, AAD), to isko samajhna thoda mushkil hai. Isliye main PDF me ise sabse aasaan bhasha me samjhaunga.
- Ise rakhne se tumhare commits 2 aur badh jaate hain, aur ye sab already bana aur test ho chuka hai.

## Mera suggestion
Rakh lo, kyunki ye ban chuka hai, live test me 11/11 pass hua hai, aur "security" ke points me madad karega. Lekin agar tum nahi samajh pa rahe ya risk nahi lena chahte, to hum isko commit na karein. Dono me se kuch bhi bologe, hum waise hi karenge.

input.content:
# Switchboard

A shared team inbox. Customers write to a business through a messaging provider
(Pigeon), support agents sign in, see conversations arrive live, claim them,
reply, and leave private notes for each other. Several workspaces share one
deployment and never see each other's data.

Stack: Node 22, Express 5, TypeScript, MongoDB, Redis, `ws`. The web app is
React + Vite.

## Run it

You need Node 22+ and Docker.

```
npm run up                  # MongoDB, Redis, Pigeon, IdP, Paybox in Docker
npm run scaffold:install    # server and web dependencies
npm run scaffold:server     # API on http://localhost:4000
npm run scaffold:web        # web app on http://localhost:5173
```

Open http://localhost:5173. Settings come from the environment; the defaults
match the local Docker services, so no `.env` is needed. `.env.example` lists
every variable. `GRADER_TOKEN` must be set explicitly when `NODE_ENV=production`.

No Docker: `npm run mocks` starts the simulators with plain Node, and
`MONGO_URL` / `REDIS_URL` can point at any MongoDB and Redis.

## Using the app

Customers are simulated by Pigeon. To make one write to you:

```
npm run inbound
```

**1. Sign in.** The app opens on a sign-in page.

![Sign in](docs/screenshots/01-sign-in.png)

**2. Pick a test user.** The identity provider is a mock, so there are no
passwords: click a user. Ben Ortiz is an agent in `ws_acme`; Eli Novak belongs
to two workspaces and gets a workspace switcher.

![Identity provider](docs/screenshots/02-identity-provider.png)

**3. The inbox.** Conversations are listed with the newest activity first.
Use the Open, Closed and Mine tabs to filter. Each row shows the last message
and who holds the conversation.

![Inbox](docs/screenshots/03-inbox.png)

**4. Read a conversation.** Click a row. Customer messages are on the left, in
the order they were sent.

![Conversation](docs/screenshots/04-conversation.png)

**5. Claim it and reply.** Claim puts your name on the conversation; nobody else
can claim it until you release it. Type a reply and press Enter. The message
shows its status as it goes: queued, sent, delivered (or failed).

![Claim and reply](docs/screenshots/05-claim-and-reply.png)

**6. Leave a private note.** Open "Private notes" and add one. Notes are
encrypted in the browser, so the server stores text it cannot read. See
`PROTOCOL.md`.

![Private note](docs/screenshots/06-private-note.png)

**7. Watch it update live.** When a customer writes, the list and the open
conversation update without a refresh. If the connection drops, the app
reconnects and catches up on what it missed.

![Live update](docs/screenshots/07-live-update.png)

**8. Close a conversation.** Closed conversations move to the Closed tab. A new
message from the customer reopens them.

![Closed tab](docs/screenshots/08-closed-tab.png)

## Check and tests

```
npm run check               # level 1, about 90 s
npm run check:full          # levels 1, 2, 3 and 5, about 4 min, writes CHECK_REPORT.json
npm run check -- --levels 5
npm --prefix scaffold/server test    # unit and integration tests (needs MongoDB and Redis)
```

The check starts the server itself (see `switchboard.json`), so stop your dev
server first. It wipes application data. The tests use a separate database
(`switchboard_test`).

`CHECK_REPORT.json` is the result of the last full run: 75 of 75 on levels 1, 2,
3 and 5. Level 4 (the written rules) is not part of the local check.

## How it is put together

```
Pigeon --webhook--> POST /webhooks/pigeon --> MongoDB (messages, frames)
                                                  |
                          Redis pub/sub  <--------+
                                |
browser <--WebSocket /ws--------+

agent reply --> outbox (MongoDB) --> sender loop --> Pigeon /v1/messages
```

- **Webhooks** (`routes/webhook.ts`): HMAC signature over the raw body, five
  minute window. A message is stored first and acknowledged after, so a
  crash makes Pigeon retry. Inserts are keyed on Pigeon's `message_id`, so
  duplicates collapse. Order is by `occurred_at`, not arrival.
- **Frames** (`lib/frames.ts`): every change a client may care about is a row
  with a per-workspace `seq`, written under a short Redis lock so rows commit
  in seq order. WebSocket clients read rows after their last seq, which is
  also how `?after=` replay works.
- **Replies** (`lib/outbox.ts`): a reply is a row in `outbox`, written before
  the request is answered. Any server copy can lease a due row (20 s lease),
  so work left by a dead copy is picked up by the others. Pigeon gets the
  `client_ref` as `Idempotency-Key`, which makes every retry safe.
- **Rate limit** (`lib/ratelimit.ts`): one token bucket per workspace in
  Redis, shared by all copies. A `429 Retry-After` or `503` pauses the
  workspace for everyone.
- **Claim** (`lib/conversations.ts`): one atomic upsert guarded by a unique
  index on `(workspace, contact)`, so only one agent can hold a conversation.
- **Login** (`lib/oidc.ts`, `routes/auth.ts`): authorization code with PKCE,
  the id_token is checked against the IdP's keys, the session lives in Redis.
  Every API call and the WebSocket check workspace membership.
- **Private notes** (`routes/notes.ts`, `scaffold/web/src/crypto.ts`): keys are
  made and used in the browser only; the server stores ciphertext.

## Layout

```
scaffold/server/src
  index.ts            wiring, health, shutdown
  config.ts           environment
  db.ts               collections and indexes
  ws.ts               WebSocket server
  routes/             webhook, auth, api, notes, grader (check endpoints)
  lib/                signature, frames, inbound, outbox, ratelimit,
                      conversations, oidc, session, cookies
scaffold/server/test  tests
scaffold/web/src      React app (components/, crypto.ts, keyring.ts, useSocket.ts)
harness/              the check (given)
pigeon/ idp/ paybox/  simulators (given)
docs/screenshots      images used above
```

`DECISIONS.md` has what was cut and what is still wrong. `PROTOCOL.md` describes
the notes encryption.

and who holds the conversation.

content.text:
Dono kaam ho gaye hain.

## 1. Screenshot wale sawaal ka jawab
Haan, Claude Code me `/export` command hai. Ye conversation ko file me ya clipboard me save kar deta hai. Ye tumhe khud apne session me chalana hoga, main isse nahi chala sakta.

Asli round ke liye:
- **`ai-logs/` zaroori hai.** Saari AI sessions ka export `ai-logs/` me daalna hai, bina edit kiye. Warna AI ke 3 points 0 aur manual review.
- **Honest rehna:** logs me saaf dikhega ki code kaun likh raha tha. "AI jaisa na lage" wali strategy kaam nahi karegi aur risky hai. Sahi tareeka ye hai ki code tumhe samajh aaye, aur follow-up call me tum use explain kar sako. Allowed hai AI use karna, bas chhupana nahi hai.
- Is practice repo me `ai-logs/` nahi hai, kyunki ye practice hai.

## 2. Commits push ho gaye
GitHub pe ab 8 commits hain (`c55e96e` latest), sab Supriya Kumari ke naam se:

| Commit | Message |
|---|---|
| `da657b6` | web: inbox, thread, reply, claim, live updates |
| `7422af7` | server: encrypted notes endpoints, key sharing and tests |
| `e1accae` | web: encrypted private notes and protocol notes |
| `c55e96e` | docs: decisions, readme with screenshots, check report |

README me ab 8 screenshots step-wise hain. Wo maine real Chrome browser se khud liye, isliye UI pehli baar sach me test bhi ho gayi: login, claim, reply (`delivered`), encrypted note, live update, aur close sab chale.

## 3. Reviewer agent
GoHighLevel hiring panel ki tarah kaam kar raha hai. Wo pushed repo ko padhega, bugs dhundhega, tests aur build chalayega (par `check` nahi), aur batayega: **shortlist hoga ya nahi**, har rubric line pe estimated score, top risks, follow-up call ke 6 sawal, aur kya karne se verdict behtar hoga. Uska report aate hi main tumhe bata dunga, aur jo real problems nikalenge wo fix karunga.

PDF aur search/billing ke "enhancements" reviewer ke result ke baad.

UI toh bahut bekaar banaya hai bhai thoda professional bana and designer se banwa dekh baaki sb kaise banate hai. aisi chize product manager se review krwa and fir banwa taaki ye sab decision v ham likh paaye accordingly smjh rhe ho

Samajh gaya, UI tumhe basic lag rahi hai. Process ye rakhunga: pehle ek **Product Manager agent** current UI ko review karega aur batayega ki ek inbox me kya hona chahiye. Saath hi ek **Designer agent** ek proper design direction dega (rang, fonts, layout, spacing, states). Dono parallel chalenge. Phir unke decisions ke hisaab se UI build hogi, aur wahi decisions `DECISIONS.md` me likhe jayenge.

input.description: Product manager review of inbox UI
input.prompt:
You are a senior Product Manager who has shipped shared team inbox / customer messaging products (think Front, Intercom, Help Scout, Zendesk, Crisp, GoHighLevel's Conversations). Review the first version of "Switchboard", a shared team inbox, and write a product review and a prioritised change list for the next iteration of the web UI. Read-only: do NOT edit any file.

Product (from /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/gohlai-assessment/BRIEF.md, read it): customers write to a business over a messaging provider (SMS-style, phone numbers as contacts); support agents (humans at the business) sign in via an identity provider, see conversations arrive in real time, claim a conversation (only one holder), reply (status: queued, sent, delivered, failed), close/reopen, and leave end-to-end encrypted private notes for teammates. Several workspaces (businesses) are isolated; some users belong to two. It is judged as a hiring assessment for GoHighLevel, so the UI should look like a credible product a small support team could use on day one, but it is built in a few hours, so scope must be realistic: no new backend work except tiny, clearly justified additions.

Look at the current UI: screenshots in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/docs/screenshots/*.png (open them with the Read tool; 01 sign-in, 02 identity provider, 03 inbox, 04 conversation, 05 claim+reply, 06 private note, 07 live update, 08 closed tab) and the code in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/web/src (App.tsx, components/*, styles.css). The API it can use is in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/server/src/routes/api.ts and notes.ts. Currently the conversation list shows only the raw phone number, a preview, a relative time and an assignee chip; there is no avatar, no unread state, no timestamps grouped by day, no way to search, no empty-state guidance, no toasts, no keyboard shortcuts, minimal visual hierarchy.

Deliver (under 800 words, plain language):
1. THE USER AND THEIR JOB: who uses this, what they do in the first 5 minutes of a shift, and the 3 moments that matter most (e.g. "new message arrives", "who owns this").
2. WHAT FEELS UNPROFESSIONAL OR WEAK TODAY: 8 specific problems seen in the screenshots/code, ranked by user impact.
3. PRIORITISED CHANGES: a numbered list, each with: the change, why (user value), effort (S/M/L for a frontend-only change), and an acceptance criterion a reviewer can check by looking at a screenshot. Mark MUST / SHOULD / COULD. Only include things that work with the existing API (or say exactly which tiny field would be needed). Consider: contact avatars with initials and colour, unread/new-message indicator, grouping messages by day with separators, message status icons, 'claimed by <name>' shown with the person's name where available, clearer claim/close actions, a conversation info panel, search/filter by phone number or text on the client side, sensible empty states, loading skeletons, error toasts, connection indicator, keyboard shortcuts, accessibility (contrast, focus), responsive behaviour.
4. WHAT TO DELIBERATELY NOT BUILD in this iteration and why (this goes into the project's DECISIONS file).
5. 5 PRODUCT DECISIONS to record, each as one sentence: 'We chose X over Y because Z'.
Be concrete and opinionated; no generic advice.

input.description: UI designer: visual design spec
input.prompt:
You are a senior product designer (UI/UX) who designs SaaS inbox products. Produce a concrete visual design specification for the web UI of "Switchboard", a shared team inbox (customers message a business by SMS-style messages; support agents claim conversations, reply with delivery status, close/reopen, and leave private encrypted notes). Read-only: do NOT edit any file in the repo; you may write your spec only as your final answer.

Look at the current UI first: screenshots in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/docs/screenshots/*.png (open with the Read tool: 01 sign-in, 02 identity provider [third party, ignore], 03 inbox, 04 conversation, 05 claim+reply, 06 private note, 07 live update, 08 closed tab) and the current code/CSS in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/web/src (App.tsx, components/*, styles.css) so your spec maps onto real components: SignIn, TopBar, Workspace, Inbox, ConversationRow, Thread, ThreadHeader, MessageBubble, ReplyBox, NotesPanel, Banner. It is currently a plain grey/white layout with a blue primary, system font, little hierarchy. Reference the visual language of modern inbox products (Front, Intercom, Linear-style restraint, Help Scout, Slack) but do not copy any brand. Constraint: implementation must be plain CSS + React with inline SVG icons (no UI framework, no icon package, no CSS framework); fonts must be system fonts or a single Google font loaded via a link tag is NOT allowed (offline-safe): use a system font stack. Must support keyboard focus visibility and WCAG AA contrast. Support light mode; dark mode optional via prefers-color-scheme if cheap.

Deliver a spec an engineer can implement directly (under 1000 words):
1. DESIGN PRINCIPLES (3, one line each) and the product's personality.
2. DESIGN TOKENS as CSS custom properties: full colour palette (background layers, surface, border, text primary/secondary/muted, brand/accent with hover/active, success/warning/danger, plus the colours for message states and for the 'private note' yellow), 8 avatar colours for initials, spacing scale, radii, shadows, type scale (sizes/weights/line-heights), z-index/layout widths (sidebar, list column, thread, optional right info panel). Give exact hex values and px/rem values.
3. LAYOUT: describe the screen structure (e.g. narrow left rail with workspace switcher, conversation list column, thread column, optional info panel) with widths and breakpoints, and what collapses on small screens.
4. COMPONENT SPECS for each component above: structure, sizes, states (default/hover/selected/focus/disabled/loading/empty/error), and details: conversation row (avatar initials, name or formatted phone number, preview, time, assignee chip with initials, unread dot/bold), thread header (contact, formatted phone, status pill, claim/release/close buttons hierarchy: one primary action), day separators, message bubbles (inbound vs outbound, grouping consecutive messages, timestamp and delivery status icons: clock, single check, double check, error with retry hint), composer (auto-grow textarea, send button with keyboard hint, character count near the limit), private note styling and the lock/encrypted treatment, banners/toasts, connection indicator, skeleton loaders, empty states with short friendly copy, sign-in page (centered card with brand mark, one-line value proposition, primary button).
5. MOTION: 3 tiny micro-interactions with durations/easing (new message arrives, status change, panel open), and prefers-reduced-motion handling.
6. COPY: exact microcopy for empty states, errors, buttons, tooltips.
7. 5 DESIGN DECISIONS to record as one sentence each: 'We chose X over Y because Z'.
Be specific with numbers and values; no vague adjectives.

  SWITCHBOARD v1 PRODUCT REVIEW AND V2 WEB UI CHANGE LIST
  
  Evidence base: screenshots 03, 05 and 06; ConversationRow, ThreadHeader, TopBar, Workspace, MessageBubble, Banner, Inbox and styles.css; api.ts and notes.ts. A few things limit what is possible. The API returns only `sub` ids for assignees and senders, and only the signed-in user's own name (`/api/me`). It has no read or unread state, no contact names, and no search parameter. Anything that needs those must be client-side or needs a tiny addition, flagged below.
  
  1. THE USER AND THEIR JOB
  The user is a support agent on a 2 to 6 person team. They sit at a desktop with the inbox open all day, and one in five of them also covers a second workspace.
  
  First 5 minutes of a shift:
  - See what came in overnight.
  - Skip what a teammate already owns.
  - Claim the oldest unanswered conversation and reply.
  - Check that earlier replies actually went out.
  
  The 3 moments that matter:
  - **New message arrives.** The agent needs to notice it without staring at the list. Which conversation is it, and is it mine?
  - **Who owns this?** Before typing, the agent must see a name, not an id, and know whether they can reply or must claim first. A double reply to a customer is the worst failure.
  - **Did my reply land?** The agent needs to trust the sent, delivered and failed states, and to retry a failure.
  
  2. WHAT FEELS WEAK TODAY (ranked by user impact)
  1. The assignee shows as a raw id like "u_ben" in rows and in "Held by u_ben". Ownership is the core job, and it reads as debug output.
  2. There is no unread or "new since I looked" signal. Screenshot 07 shows live updates, but a row only changes its text, so the agent cannot tell what is new.
  3. Rows are raw phone numbers with no avatar, so 20 rows look identical. Every row also says "now" and "Unassigned" in the same grey pill, so nothing stands out.
  4. Failed sends are only a subtle bubble tint plus the word "failed". There is no retry and no explanation (the ReplyBox shows no inline error).
  5. Claim, Release and Close are three equal-weight buttons. The disabled Claim button is grey (screenshot 05). The header never says why the Claim button is disabled, and Close sits next to Release with no confirmation or undo.
  6. The thread has no day separators, and the time is shown as 18:57 on every bubble. Status is plain text, not an icon.
  7. The private notes block is a heading with "(show)" and takes up the whole top of the thread when open (screenshot 06). It pushes the conversation down, and the yellow note looks like a message.
  8. There is no search, no empty-state guidance ("Select a conversation to read it", and a blank list under Closed), no skeletons, no toasts, and a thin info banner for connection loss. Also: the workspace picker shows raw ids (`ws_acme`) and there is no responsive layout. Muted text (#667085 on #f6f7f9) and the faint disabled Send button are borderline on contrast.
  
  3. PRIORITISED CHANGES
  Effort is S, M or L for frontend only.
  
  MUST
  1. **Name resolution.** Map each `sub` to a display name: me from `/api/me`, others from a name map, falling back to "Teammate (u_be…)". Tiny backend addition: put `name` on the key members returned by the notes keys endpoint, because the server already knows names from login; that endpoint is the only existing member list. Effort M with the addition. Acceptance: the row and header read "Ben Ortiz", never `u_ben`.
  2. **Avatars and row layout.** Initials in a coloured circle (hash of the phone number into 8 colours). The phone number is formatted `+1 (415) 555-0101`. Add a separate assignee avatar or "You" chip, and a timestamp that becomes a day label after 24h. Effort S. Acceptance: a screenshot of 4 rows shows 4 distinguishable avatars and formatted numbers.
  3. **Unread dot.** Keep a last-seen timestamp per contact in localStorage. A `message.inbound` frame for a non-selected contact bolds the row, shows a blue dot, and moves it to the top. Opening the conversation clears it. No backend change (the preview and `lastActivityAt` already arrive). Effort M. Acceptance: with conversation A open, a message to B gives B a bold row and a dot (screenshot 07 style).
  4. **Ownership bar in the thread.** The header says "Claimed by Ben Ortiz" or "Unclaimed". The primary action is a single filled **Claim** button. When someone else holds it, show a locked state "Ben Ortiz is handling this" and a disabled composer with the reason. Effort M. Acceptance: viewed as a non-holder, the reply box is disabled and the reason is visible without a tooltip.
  5. **Failed send handling.** Failed bubbles get a red border, an alert icon, an inline "Failed to send. Retry" button that reuses the same `clientRef`, and a toast on failure. Effort M. Acceptance: a failed bubble shows the label and the retry control.
  6. **Day separators and status ticks.** Add "Today", "Yesterday" and date separators, and group consecutive bubbles. Replace status words with icons plus an accessible label (clock for queued, one tick for sent, two ticks for delivered, red alert for failed). Effort S. Acceptance: separator visible, and each status distinguishable in grayscale.
  
  SHOULD
  7. **Toasts and the connection pill.** Add a toast container for claim conflicts ("Ben already claimed this"), close/reopen results and API errors. Replace the banner with a small status dot in the top bar: green Live, amber Reconnecting. Effort S. Acceptance: a 409 on claim produces a toast, not silence.
  8. **Client-side search.** An input above the list filters the loaded rows by phone digits or preview text. Label it "Search loaded conversations" so it is not mistaken for full search. Effort S. Acceptance: typing "4821" or "0102" narrows the list.
  9. **Skeletons and empty states.** Skeleton rows while loading. Empty copy per tab ("No open conversations. New customer messages appear here live", "You have not claimed anything. Open a conversation and press Claim"). A first-time empty-thread panel with 3 tips. Effort S. Acceptance: each of the three tabs shows distinct text when empty.
  10. **Notes as a side tab.** Move notes into a tabbed panel "Reply | Private note" attached to the composer, with a lock icon, a yellow tint on the composer, and the note timeline interleaved visually with a "Private" label. Effort M. Acceptance: the thread keeps its full height with notes open.
  11. **Info panel (right column or drawer).** Shows the number, status, owner, message count and first-contact date, all derived from loaded messages. Effort M. Acceptance: it opens from the header and shows the owner's name.
  12. **Accessibility.** Darken muted text to #475467 or better (contrast of at least 4.5:1). Make the disabled Send visible and explain why, add focus rings on rows, add a skip link, and give the list `aria-live="polite"` announcements. Effort S.
  
  COULD
  13. **Keyboard shortcuts:** `j`/`k` move, `c` claim, `e` close, `/` search, `Esc` back, `?` help. Effort M. Acceptance: a help dialog lists them.
  14. **Responsive layout:** below 800px show list or thread, with a Back button. Effort M.
  15. **Workspace switcher:** show names, not ids, as a menu in the top bar. Effort S.
  16. **Sound or tab-title count** for unread, for example "(3) Switchboard". Effort S.
  
  4. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT (for DECISIONS)
  - **Server-side unread and read receipts.** They need a per-user read-state schema and extra WebSocket frames; local state covers one agent on one device for now.
  - **Server-side search (Elasticsearch)** and contact names or CRM fields. The brief lists search as a separate valued item, and the client-side filter only covers loaded rows.
  - **Canned replies, tags, snooze, SLA timers, and analytics.** Each is a product of its own, and none is exercised by the claim, reply or note flow.
  - **Attachments and emoji.** The provider is SMS-style text only.
  - **Drag to reassign, a transfer UI, and bulk actions.** The race-safe claim exists, and transfer should go through release then claim.
  - **Dark mode and theming.** It adds cost and no function.
  - **Typing indicators and presence.** They need new WebSocket frames, and customers are simulated.
  - **Note editing and deletion.** This complicates the encryption protocol.
  
  5. PRODUCT DECISIONS
  1. We chose client-side unread state in localStorage over a server read-model because it needs no backend change and the single-device agent is the common case.
  2. We chose to show people by display name, with a name field added to the existing member list, over adding a new directory endpoint, because it is a one-field change that fixes the biggest trust problem.
  3. We chose a locked composer when another agent holds a conversation over allowing a reply with a warning, because duplicate replies to a customer cannot be undone.
  4. We chose Retry that reuses the same `clientRef` over a new send because the server de-duplicates by that ref, so a retry can never reach the customer twice.
  5. We chose search over loaded conversations only, clearly labelled, over faking full-text search, because honest limits beat a misleading result and Elasticsearch search is a separate valued item.

cd ~/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard/scaffold/server/src && grep -n "first registration\|first-write\|first write" ../../../PROTOCOL.md | cut -c1-140; python3 - <<'EOF'
def sub(path, old, new, count=1):
    s = open(path).read()
    assert old in s, (path, old[:60])
    open(path, 'w').write(s.replace(old, new, count))

# pagination: _id cursor must be an ObjectId, not a string
sub('routes/api.ts', "import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';", "import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';\nimport { ObjectId } from 'mongodb';")
sub('routes/api.ts', "  if (before && before.length === 2 && !Number.isNaN(Number(before[0]))) {\n    const t = new Date(Number(before[0]));\n    filter.$or = [{ lastActivityAt: { $lt: t } }, { lastActivityAt: t, _id: { $lt: before[1] } }];\n  }",
"  if (before && before.length === 2 && !Number.isNaN(Number(before[0])) && ObjectId.isValid(before[1])) {\n    const t = new Date(Number(before[0]));\n    filter.$or = [{ lastActivityAt: { $lt: t } }, { lastActivityAt: t, _id: { $lt: new ObjectId(before[1]) } }];\n  }")

# a malformed cookie must not turn into a 500
sub('lib/cookies.ts', "    out[part.slice(0, i).trim()] = decodeURIComponent(part.slice(i + 1).trim());",
"    const raw = part.slice(i + 1).trim();\n    try {\n      out[part.slice(0, i).trim()] = decodeURIComponent(raw);\n    } catch {\n      out[part.slice(0, i).trim()] = raw;\n    }")

# origin checks on the websocket upgrade and logout
sub('ws.ts', "      const session = await sessionFromCookie(req.headers.cookie);", "      const origin = req.headers.origin;\n      if (origin && origin !== config.webOrigin && origin !== `http://${req.headers.host}`) return reject(socket, '403 Forbidden');\n      const session = await sessionFromCookie(req.headers.cookie);")
sub('routes/auth.ts', "auth.post('/auth/logout', async (req, res) => {", "auth.post('/auth/logout', async (req, res) => {\n  const origin = req.header('origin');\n  if (origin && origin !== config.webOrigin && origin !== `http://${req.header('host')}`) return res.status(403).json({ error: 'bad origin' });")

# an unexpected 4xx is retried a few times before the reply is given up on
sub('lib/outbox.ts', "  // 4xx other than 429 will not get better by trying again\n", "  // other 4xx is probably final, but give a transient auth or conflict error a few tries\n  if (doc.attempts < 5) return retryLater();\n")
EOF
cd .. && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | head; echo tsc-done

  - No selection: "Pick a conversation to start."
  - Empty thread: "No messages yet."
  - Empty notes: "No notes yet. Add context only your team can see."

  2. We chose a single indigo accent with a neutral palette over per-state rainbow colours because state is carried by icon + text and the brand stays for the one primary action.
  3. We chose filled outbound bubbles and white inbound bubbles over same-colour bubbles because direction is readable at a glance, and the two contrast pairs both meet AA.

  5. We chose yellow tint + a left bar + a lock icon for notes over a separate tab because notes stay visible in context and can never be mistaken for a message sent to the customer.

  - New message: translateY(8px) + opacity 0 to 1, 180ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`. A new row in the list flashes `--brand-soft` for 600ms.

  - Panel open (info drawer, notes): width/translateX 220ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, with the scrim fading over 150ms.

  ## 6. Copy
  - Empty list (Open): "All caught up. New messages will show up here."; (Mine): "Nothing assigned to you. Claim a conversation to get started."; (Closed): "No closed conversations yet."
  - No selection: "Pick a conversation to start."
  - Empty thread: "No messages yet."
  - Empty notes: "No notes yet. Add context only your team can see."
  - Errors: "Couldn't load conversations. Try again" (button Retry); "Message not delivered. Retry"; "Couldn't send. Check your connection."; "Someone else claimed this first."; "Can't decrypt this note on this device."
  - Buttons: Claim, Release, Close conversation, Reopen, Send, Add note, Sign in with your work account, Sign out.
  - Tooltips: "Send (Enter)", "Sent", "Delivered", "Sending...", "Not delivered. Click to retry", "Encrypted. Only your team can read this", "Live", "Reconnecting...", "Offline".
  - Sign-in tagline: "One shared inbox for every customer text."
  
  ## 7. Decisions
  1. We chose a dark narrow rail over a top bar because it frees 48px of vertical space for messages and gives the workspace and user a stable home.
  2. We chose a single indigo accent with a neutral palette over per-state rainbow colours because state is carried by icon + text and the brand stays for the one primary action.
  3. We chose filled outbound bubbles and white inbound bubbles over same-colour bubbles because direction is readable at a glance, and the two contrast pairs both meet AA.
  4. We chose system fonts and inline SVG over a webfont or icon pack because the app must work offline with zero added dependencies.

content.text:
Reviewer ka verdict, jo fix hua, aur UI ka status, sab ek jagah.

## Reviewer ka verdict: BORDERLINE, ~70% confidence, estimated ~80/100
Engineering ko usne strong bataya (frames, outbox, rate limit, signature). Do badi baatein:

1. **`ai-logs/` nahi hai.** Asli round me ye sabse bada gap hoga: AI ke 3 points 0 aur manual review. Ye sirf tum bhar sakte ho (`/export` se).
2. **Commit history.** Kai commits ka timestamp ek jaisa hai (batch me banaye the). Asli round me ek-ek feature ke baad turant commit karo (har ~15 min), warna history "batched" lagegi. Timestamps ko badalna ya backdate karna mat, wo dhokha hoga.

## Jo bugs reviewer ne pakde aur maine fix kiye
- Inbox pagination me `_id` ka compare galat tha, to page ki seema pe rows chhoot sakti thi.
- Kharaab cookie se 500 aata tha.
- WebSocket aur logout pe Origin check nahi tha.
- Ek ajeeb 4xx pe reply turant "failed" ho jata tha, ab 5 try ke baad hota hai.
- `PROTOCOL.md` me ek real attack saaf likha (server naye member ko nakli workspace key de sakta hai).
- Naye tests: webhook ke saare rules aur outbox idempotency. Ab **41 tests pass**.

Reviewer ke do points maine jaan-boojhkar nahi badle: seq ka Redis lock (isse frames order me commit hote hain, aur unique index backup hai) aur sender ka "ek tick me ek row" (asli rok token bucket hai, tick nahi).

## UI redesign
PM aur Designer ke reports aa gaye. Maine unhe milakar ek brief diya, aur implementer abhi kaam kar raha hai:
- Dark narrow rail, avatars, naam (`Ben Ortiz`, `u_ben` nahi), unread dot, day separators, status icons, search, skeleton, toasts, aur notes ke liye side panel.
- PM aur designer me do jagah mismatch tha: PM ne dark mode na banane ko kaha aur designer ne cheap bataya. Maine dark mode **chhoda**. Notes ko main right panel me rakha, taaki thread ki height na ghate.
- Ek jagah mujhe PM ki salah me galti dikhi: "Retry me wahi clientRef" failed message pe kaam nahi karta, kyunki server us ref ko duplicate maan lega. Isliye failed message ka retry **naye ref** se jata hai.

Implementer ke baad: main build verify karunga, naye screenshots lunga, full check chalaunga, aur DECISIONS/README update karunga. Phir naye commits (fixes aur UI) tumhari confirmation ke baad.

pkill -f "tsx src/index.ts"; pkill -f vite; sleep 1; cd ~/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='DECISIONS.md'
s=open(p).read()
a="## Choices where the brief is silent"
b="""## Product and design decisions (inbox UI)

Before redesigning the UI I had it reviewed from a product and from a design point of view, and kept the decisions that came out of it.

- Unread state lives in the browser (localStorage), not on the server. It needs no backend change, and an agent mostly works from one device. A server read-model would be the next step.
- People are shown by name, not by id. The one small backend addition for this is `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/people`.
- When another agent holds a conversation the reply box is locked with the reason written next to it, rather than allowing a reply with a warning. A duplicate reply to a customer cannot be taken back.
- Retry on a failed message sends it as a new message with a new `client_ref`. The server dedupes on `client_ref`, so reusing the old one would not resend. Only a request that got no answer at all is retried with the same ref.
- Search covers the conversations already loaded and is labelled that way, instead of pretending to be full-text search. Real search is the Elasticsearch item.
- A dark narrow rail on the left (workspace, connection state, account) instead of a top bar: more room for messages. One indigo accent; state is carried by icon plus text, never colour alone.
- Private notes sit in a side panel next to the thread, not above it, so the thread keeps its height and a note cannot be mistaken for a message to the customer.
- System fonts and inline SVG only, no icon or UI library, so the app has no extra dependencies.
- Not built on purpose: dark mode, canned replies, tags, snooze, SLA timers, attachments, typing indicators, bulk actions, editing or deleting notes (that would complicate the encryption protocol).

## Choices where the brief is silent"""
assert a in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(a,b,1))
EOF

Any deployment that forgets the variable lets anyone call `POST /__grader/reset` and wipe all data. Fix: refuse to start unless the token is set, or generate a random one when unset. 7. Low: Origin check is skipped when the Origin header is absent (`api.ts:26`, `ws.ts:59`). That is fine for browsers because of SameSite=Lax. No CSRF tokens. Sessions have no `__Host-` prefix.

# Bonus track: billing

Only start this when `npm run check:full` is where you want it. It is scored
separately (10 bonus points) and never makes up for a Must tier that fails.

## The problem

Switchboard is sold per seat, per month. Build that on Paybox (`PAYBOX.md`).

1. A workspace **admin** subscribes the workspace: picks a number of seats,
   enters a card, pays. Agents cannot see or change billing.
2. Card details are entered in your UI and never touch your server.
3. The admin can change the number of seats later.
4. The app always knows the workspace's subscription state, including when it
   changes without anyone clicking anything: a renewal fails, the bank asks
   for approval, Paybox cancels after its retries run out.
5. A workspace whose subscription is **canceled** cannot send messages. It
   can still read its inbox. A workspace that has **never subscribed** is on a
   free trial and can send.
6. The admin sees the current state in plain words and what to do about it.

## Contract additions for the grader

Create the Paybox customer with `metadata.workspace` set to the workspace id.
Accept Paybox webhooks at `POST /webhooks/paybox`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /__grader/billing/subscribe` `{ workspace, seats, token }` | What your UI does when the admin submits the form, with a card token already made. `200` if the subscription is active, `402` if it is not. |
| `POST /__grader/billing/seats` `{ workspace, seats }` | Change the seat count. `200` if changed, `402` if not. |

Add to each workspace in `GET /__grader/snapshot`:

```json
"billing": { "status": "active", "seats": 3, "can_send": true }
```

`status` is `none`, `incomplete`, `active`, `past_due` or `canceled`.
When `can_send` is false, `POST /__grader/reply` for that workspace must
answer `402` and must not send.

## What the grader does

Subscribes a workspace three times in the same instant. Changes seats. Pays
for a second workspace with a card that only works once, then moves the clock
past the renewal and past the retries. Posts a forged webhook. Checks that the
canceled workspace cannot send and the paying one still can. Reads Paybox's
own record of how you called it.

## Left for you to decide (write it in DECISIONS.md)

What a `past_due` workspace is allowed to do, and for how long. What happens
to agents when seats are reduced below the number of people in the workspace.
Whether an admin who removes seats mid-month should be told about the credit.
What the UI shows while a payment is waiting for the bank.

Base URL `http://localhost:4030`. Only needed for the bonus track.

| Key | Value | Use it from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Publishable | `pk_test_paybox_9a7b3e` | The browser. Can only create card tokens. |
| Secret | `sk_test_paybox_51c0de` | Your server only. Everything else. |
| Webhook signing secret | `whsec_paybox_dev` | Your server only. |

Send keys as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Bodies are JSON. Amounts are in
cents. The one price is `price_seat_monthly`: **1200 per seat per 30 days**.

## Test cards

Any future expiry, any three-digit CVC.

| Number | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `4242 4242 4242 4242` | Always succeeds. |
| `5555 5555 5555 4444` | Always succeeds. |
| `4000 0000 0000 0002` | Every charge is declined (`card_declined`). |
| `4000 0000 0000 9995` | Every charge is declined (`insufficient_funds`). |
| `4000 0000 0000 0341` | First charge succeeds. Every later charge is declined. |
| `4000 0025 0000 3155` | First charge needs the cardholder to approve it at their bank. |
| `4000 0000 0000 0069` | Expired. Rejected when you create the token. |

1. **Browser → Paybox:** `POST /v1/tokens` with the publishable key and
   `{ "card": { "number", "exp_month", "exp_year", "cvc" } }`. You get
   `{ "id": "tok_..." }`. A token works once. Paybox counts every card number
   that reaches it through a secret key, because that means the number passed
   through somebody's server.
2. **Server → Paybox:** `POST /v1/customers` `{ name, email, metadata }`.
   Set `metadata.workspace` to the workspace id; it is how Paybox reports

3. `POST /v1/customers/:id/payment_method` `{ token }`.
4. `POST /v1/subscriptions` `{ customer, price, quantity }`.

`POST /v1/subscriptions/:id` `{ cancel_at_period_end: true }` cancels at the

  they approve or decline. You find out the result by webhook, not from that
  page.

input.prompt:
Build the WEB side of the billing bonus track for Switchboard in the ISOLATED COPY /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard-billing, only inside scaffold/web/src (React 19 + Vite + TS, plain CSS with the existing design tokens in src/styles/*.css, inline SVG icons from src/components/icons.tsx; no new dependencies). Never touch /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard, /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/gohlai-assessment, or scaffold/server (another agent is writing the server). Do not run the harness or start servers on ports 4000/5173.

First read: BONUS_BILLING.md and PAYBOX.md (card tokenization in the browser with the PUBLISHABLE key; the card number must NEVER touch our server; test cards; the 3155 card returns requires_action with a next_action.url the browser is sent to), then the current UI in src/ (App.tsx, components/Rail.tsx, Workspace.tsx, InfoPanel.tsx, ReplyBox.tsx, Thread.tsx, api.ts, types.ts, people.ts, styles/*.css) and look at docs/screenshots/05-claim-and-reply.png and 03-inbox.png to match the visual language (dark rail, indigo accent, light surfaces, calm density, system fonts).

SERVER CONTRACT you code against (the server agent is implementing it; admins only, agents get 403 on all of it):
- GET /api/billing?workspace=<id> -> { status: 'none'|'incomplete'|'active'|'past_due'|'canceled', seats: number, canSend: boolean, plainState: string, nextStep: string|null, nextActionUrl: string|null, priceCentsPerSeat: 1200, publishableKey: string, warning?: string }
- POST /api/billing/subscribe {workspace, seats, token} -> 200 { ...same shape as GET } when active; 402 { error: string, nextActionUrl?: string } when the payment did not go through (declined, or bank approval needed: then send the browser to nextActionUrl in the same tab and refresh state when the user returns).
- POST /api/billing/seats {workspace, seats} -> 200 { ...same shape, warning? } | 402 { error }
- POST /api/billing/cancel {workspace} -> 200 { ...same shape }
- For non-canceled states a reply works; for 'canceled' POST /api/conversations/:contact/reply answers 402 {error:'subscription canceled'}.
- Paybox browser tokenization: POST http://localhost:4030/v1/tokens with header Authorization: Bearer <publishableKey from GET /api/billing>, JSON body { card: { number, exp_month, exp_year, cvc } } -> { id: 'tok_...' } (read paybox/server.js to confirm the exact request/response and CORS behaviour; make the base URL a Vite env var VITE_PAYBOX_URL defaulting to http://localhost:4030).

Build:
1. A Billing screen for workspace ADMINS only: reachable from the account menu / rail (a 'Billing' item shown only when my role in the current workspace is admin; use me.workspaces[].role). Agents never see the entry, and if they navigate to it they get a short 'Only admins can manage billing' message.
2. The screen shows, in plain words: the current state sentence (plainState) with a status pill (None -> 'Free trial', Active green, Past due amber, Incomplete amber 'Waiting for payment', Canceled red), seats, monthly cost (seats x $12.00), and 'what to do next' (nextStep) as a clear call to action. Copy must be calm and plain, no jargon.
3. Subscribe form (shown for none/incomplete/canceled): seat count stepper (min 1), live total ('3 seats x $12.00 = $36.00 per month'), card form (number with spacing, expiry MM/YY, CVC; labels, autocomplete attributes cc-number/cc-exp/cc-csc, inline validation messages, Luhn is nice-to-have), a Pay button with loading state that tokenizes in the browser then POSTs only the token to our server. A line stating card details go straight to the payment provider and never to our server. Show a list of the Paybox test cards as a collapsible 'Test cards' hint (this is a demo environment): 4242 4242 4242 4242 succeeds, 4000 0000 0000 0002 declined, 4000 0000 0000 9995 insufficient funds, 4000 0000 0000 0341 first charge ok then declined at renewal, 4000 0025 0000 3155 needs bank approval.
4. Manage section when active/past_due: change seats (stepper + 'Update seats' button, shows the new total, shows the server's warning text e.g. about reducing below current team size, handles 402 with a plain message that the extra charge failed), and a 'Cancel at period end' with a confirm step.
5. States while waiting: incomplete with nextActionUrl -> a banner 'Your bank needs to approve this payment' with a button 'Approve at your bank' that navigates to the URL; poll GET /api/billing every 5 s while status is incomplete or the page was reopened after approval, stop when it changes.
6. Canceled workspace: in the thread, the ReplyBox is disabled with the visible reason 'Sending is paused because the subscription was canceled. An admin can resubscribe in Billing.' (and for admins a link to Billing). The inbox stays readable. Load billing status once per workspace for admins; for non-admins detect canceled from a 402 on reply (toast 'Sending is paused: this workspace's subscription is canceled. Ask an admin.') and disable the box from then on. Past_due: a slim amber notice at the top of the thread area for admins only.
7. Errors as toasts using the existing Toasts mechanism; all controls keyboard reachable, labelled, visible focus; reuse existing button/input classes and tokens; responsive down to 390px.

Keep code plain and human-looking (small components in src/components/billing/*, an src/billing.ts api module and hook, CSS in src/styles/billing.css imported from main.tsx), no emoji, no narration comments. Verify: `cd /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/switchboard-billing/scaffold/web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build`, then delete dist/. Re-read your own polling/cleanup and 402 handling once for bugs. Final report under 250 words: files, assumptions about the contract, anything unverified.

  **New files**
  - `src/lib/paybox.ts`: typed client. Mutating calls carry idempotency keys, and a network failure is retried once.
  - `src/lib/billing.ts`: Redis lock per workspace, subscribe, seat change, cancel, refresh from Paybox, `canSend`, and the view for the UI.
  - `src/routes/paybox.ts`: the webhook.
  - `src/routes/billing.ts`: the admin-only `/api/billing` routes.
  - `test/billing.test.ts`: the new tests.

  - `db.ts`: `billing` and `billing_events` collections with unique indexes. The grader reset already clears every collection returned by `cols()`, so both are covered.
  - `index.ts`: mounts the Paybox webhook before the JSON parsers.
  - `routes/grader.ts`: subscribe and seats endpoints, `billing` in the snapshot, and the reply gate.
  - `routes/api.ts`: mounts the billing routes and gates reply.
  - `DECISIONS.md`: new Billing section.
  
  **Decisions**
  - **past_due** can still send; Paybox cancels it after its own retries.
  - **Seats below headcount** is allowed and returns a `warning`.
  - **Seat reduction** returns a note that the unused part becomes credit and is not refunded.
  - **incomplete** can still send.
  - **incomplete_expired** maps back to `none`.
  - **Webhooks** never set state. The payload only identifies the customer, then the subscription is re-fetched. Event ids are stored after processing; duplicates get 200. Paybox or database failures return 503 so Paybox retries.
  - **Extras you didn't ask for:** a past_due workspace can submit a new card, and a failed first payment older than 5 seconds can be retried with another card (the old subscription is cancelled).
  
  **Verified by tests:** the signature check, forged/stale/unsigned webhooks (401), unknown event types (200), bad JSON (400), duplicate events, three concurrent subscribes (one customer and one subscription in Paybox), declined card (402, incomplete), the 3155 card (402 with the approval URL, then active), seat increase and decrease, a seat increase that fails (402, seats unchanged), past_due then canceled via the test clock, a canceled workspace getting 402 with nothing queued, a never-subscribed workspace sending, and agents getting 403 on billing routes.
  
  **Side effects on the simulator:** the tests advance its test clock. They do not call its reset.
  
  **Not tested:** Paybox's real webhook delivery to :4000. The simulator was not asked to send to this code, so that path is only covered by posting signed events directly.

  - **Seats below headcount** is allowed and returns a `warning`.

  - **incomplete** can still send.
  - **incomplete_expired** maps back to `none`.
  - **Webhooks** never set state. The payload only identifies the customer, then the subscription is re-fetched. Event ids are stored after processing; duplicates get 200. Paybox or database failures return 503 so Paybox retries.

## 1. Assignment kya tha

**Switchboard** ek shared team inbox hai. Socho ek shop hai jahan customers WhatsApp jaise messages bhejte hain, aur shop ke support agents un messages ka jawab dete hain.

**Kaun kaun hai:**

- **Customers**: log jo business ko message likhte hain. Yahan sab simulated (nakli) hain, Pigeon ke andar rehte hain.
- **Support agents**: business ke employees. Login karke inbox dekhte hain, conversation claim karte hain, reply dete hain, private notes likhte hain.
- **Workspaces**: alag alag businesses (`ws_acme`, `ws_globex`). Ek hi server share karte hain, par ek ka data doosre ko kabhi nahi dikhna chahiye. Jaise ek bank ke alag alag customers ke lockers.
- **Pigeon**: messaging provider (post office jaisa). Customer ke messages hum tak webhook se pahunchata hai, aur hamare replies bhejta hai. Yeh jaanbujhkar unreliable hai: duplicate, ulte order mein, jaali (forged) aur purane (replayed) messages bhejta hai, kabhi slow, kabhi down, kabhi 429 (rate limit) deta hai.

**5 levels ka check (har level ke points alag):**

| Level | Kya test hota hai | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Ek server copy. Duplicate/out-of-order/forged/stale webhooks, Pigeon slow/down/rate-limit, 6 agents ek saath claim | 24 |
| 2 | Server ko `kill -9` (achanak maar dena) aur phir start. Kuch lost, duplicate ya double-sent nahi | 14 |
| 3 | Kai copies load balancer ke peeche, shared MongoDB + Redis. Rate limit per workspace, ek copy marne par baaki 60 s mein kaam khatam karein | 22 |
| 4 | Likhe hue rules (`PIGEON.md` ki answer table). 10 rules, 1 point each. Local mein nahi chalta | 10 |
| 5 | Login (IdP), tenant isolation, WebSocket real time, kai copies ke saath | 15 |

input.prompt:
Rewrite a long study guide into a SHORT, interview-focused version for a candidate who must defend their take-home project (Switchboard, a multi-tenant shared inbox: webhooks from an unreliable provider, outbox replies, Redis rate limit, WebSocket replay, OIDC login, encrypted notes, React UI) in a live follow-up call where interviewers open the code and ask why. The candidate is not an expert, wants simple Hinglish (Roman Hindi mixed with English tech words, short sentences, friendly), and wants ONLY what helps in the interview: what they can be asked, how to understand it, and how to answer aloud. No fluff, no history lessons.

Inputs (read all three, then condense; keep facts exactly consistent with the code in /Users/apple/Desktop/repo-new/gohlai-assessment, do not invent): /tmp/pdf-parts/A.md, /tmp/pdf-parts/B.md, /tmp/pdf-parts/C.md. Write ONLY /tmp/pdf-parts/short.md (Markdown). HARD LIMIT: about 3500 words total (it must print to 10-12 pages). Do not edit repo files.

Structure (use `##` headings):
1. '2 minute pitch' - what to say first (6-8 lines): problem, architecture in one sentence each for inbound, outbound, realtime, auth, UI; the check result (75/75 on levels 1,2,3,5; level 4 hand-verified); tests count; what is deliberately not done.
2. 'System ek picture me' - the small ASCII diagram and one line per box.
3. '10 concepts jo zaroor samajhne hain' - each 4-5 lines max in this fixed format: **Kya** (1 line, with analogy) / **Kyun** (1 line) / **Code** (file:function) / **Ek line me bolna**. Concepts: webhook signature + 5-minute rule; idempotent store + ack after store; outbox + lease + Idempotency-Key; Redis token bucket + Retry-After; claim race with unique index; seq frames + WebSocket replay; OIDC + PKCE + sessions; tenant isolation + origin checks; encrypted notes (who holds which key, 3 attacks not stopped); the retry rule (new client_ref for failed vs same for no-answer).
4. 'Interview me ye poochh sakte hain (18 sawal)' - question, then a 3-line answer in spoken style, then 'Dikhana: file:function'. Pick the 18 MOST likely and most dangerous: kill -9 windows, double send on timeout, lock vs counter for seq, pagination cursor weakness, Origin vs SameSite, hostile server vs notes, what is still wrong, why Redis AND Mongo, how does failover work across copies, why Express 5, how is tenant isolation enforced, NoSQL injection, why per-workspace rate limit, how unread works, what the people endpoint is, why a GET must not write, what you would build next, what you would change with 2 more days.
5. 'Code badlo' - a compact table of 6 likely live changes: change | file | what to edit.
6. 'Weak points - seedha bolna' - the honest known weaknesses (from DECISIONS.md) each as one line plus the one-line fix you would make.
7. 'AI ke baare me kya bolna hai' - a short honest script (5-6 lines): used Claude Code with sub-agents for implementation and reviews; the candidate set the requirements, made the decisions, ran the checks/tests/browser runs, and acted on review findings; can explain every part; AI transcripts are in ai-logs/. No defensiveness, nothing hidden.
8. 'Numbers aur commands' - tiny table: lease 20 s, token bucket 3.5/s burst 6, webhook window 5 min, send timeout 6 s, session 8 h, frame lock 3 s, tests count; commands: npm run up, npm run check:full, npm --prefix scaffold/server test.
Check the test count and other numbers against the repo before writing. Final message: one line saying the file is written and the word count.

Abhi **19:28** hai. Ye poora hisaab hai.

## GitHub pe commit ho chuka hai (10 commits, sab `main` pe)
| # | Kya |
|---|---|
| 1 | Server: webhook, outbox, rate limit, claim |
| 2 | README (run steps, architecture) |
| 3 | Login, API, WebSocket |
| 4 | Frontend: inbox, thread, reply, claim, live updates |
| 5 | Server: encrypted notes endpoints + tests |
| 6 | Web: encrypted notes + `PROTOCOL.md` |
| 7 | Docs: decisions, README screenshots, check report |
| 8 | Server hardening: pagination fix, origin checks, names endpoint, contact validation, 43 tests |
| 9 | Web: naya UI (rail, avatars, unread, details/notes panel) |
| 10 | Docs final: decisions, protocol, naye screenshots, check report (75/75) |

Matlab **poora core project, UI, notes, tests aur docs GitHub pe hain**, aur wo 75/75 pe verified hai.

## Abhi commit NAHI hua
1. **`ai-logs/`** repo ke folder me hai (uncommitted). Ye sabse zaroori hai. Commit tab karenge jab aakhri baar transcript refresh ho jaye. Pehle ek version abhi push kar dena safe rahega.
2. **Billing (bonus)**: alag copy `switchboard-billing` me ready hai. Server (54 tests) aur web build pass, full check 75/75. `main` me merge nahi hua. Abhi browser me billing UI dekhna baaki hai.
3. **README me chhoti galti:** "41 tests" likha hai, sach me 43 hain.

## Repo se bahar (GitHub pe nahi jayega)
- **PDF guide**, 31 pages ka. Tumne chhota karne ko kaha, uska agent abhi chal raha hai (~10-12 pages, sirf interview ke hisaab se).

## Abhi baaki kaam
| Kaam | Kab |
|---|---|
| Billing UI browser me dekhna, phir merge ya skip ka faisla | Abhi |
| README ka test count theek karna | Merge ke saath |
| Final `check:full` | Merge ke baad |
| `ai-logs/` aakhri refresh + commit | Sabse last |
| Repo public karna + form bharna | ~7:55 se pehle |
